whys: Mining does not affect card lifespan; clean cards run faster.
Used cards do not perform worse than new ones.

comments.author: scambier
comments.why: Used cards do not perform worse than new ones.
comments.text: There's a nice Linus Tech Tips video about this: [VIDEO] The tl;dw is that used cards don't perform worse than new cards - your card either works, or it doesn't. But like any electronics, they have an "expiration date", and if it's been used for 2 years, it's 2 years closer to dying. It's up to you to decide if the discount of a used card might be worth it.

comments.author: bentcorner
comments.why: Mining does not affect card lifespan; clean cards run faster.
comments.text: LTT goes over it pretty well (IMO): [VIDEO] tldr: Cards (like any piece of other electronics) do have a lifespan, but mining doesn't affect that. Cards that are kept clean and in better working conditions will run faster.

comments.author: ulrikrasmussen
comments.story: GPU mining no longer profitable after Ethereum merge
comments.why: LTT found performance degradation from mining insignificant; dust cooling risk.
comments.text: Linus tech tips had an episode on it, and largely found that the performance degradation was insignificant: [VIDEO] He did however note that the cards that he tested had been used in a relatively clean and dust-free environment. The biggest risk to buying a card that has been running 24/7 for years is that the cooling system is busted due to build-up of dust.

comments.author: belthesar
comments.why: LMG testing found mining GPUs worked fine.
comments.text: This is but one test, but Linus Media Group did some testing and found that mining GPUs worked just fine. Fan time and thermal pad degradation are about the only real detractors from buying a used GPU. [VIDEO] Of course, if a card's running at thermal throttle for long periods of time, that has a chance to damage the card, but given that most cards are running underclocked, the likelihood that you'll run into that problem is low.

comments.author: kevingadd
comments.story: Bitcoin Falls Below $20k for the First Time Since 2020
comments.why: Tests show mining does not meaningfully damage GPUs.
comments.text: A few different people have done tests to verify whether GPUs used for eth mining took any damage from doing so, and haven't managed to find any evidence that it damages the card more than regular use. Running cards under severe load nonstop for years could potentially shorten their lifespan by a tiny bit due to electromigration or wear out the fans, but that's about it. Of course, any used GPU could be defective, so you need to be careful buying one no matter what. [VIDEO] [LINK]
